title: Inverse image of Tate twists
statement:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let
$\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb\}$ be admissible. There are canonical
isomorphisms
$$
f^{-1}\mu_{\ell^n,Y}\cong\mu_{\ell^n,X},\qquad
f^{-1}\bigl(\Lambda_Y(d)\bigr)\cong\Lambda_X(d)\quad(d\in\mathbf Z),
$$
compatible with the isomorphism $\alpha_f\colon f^{-1}\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_X$ of
[lem-sfb-alpha-iso] and the module structures, and with the Kummer transition maps.
Consequently $f^*(K(d))\cong(f^*K)(d)$ for $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.

proof.text:
Representables on the small pro-etale sites. Use the compatible small skeleta and larger sheaf universe in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For an object $V\to Y$ of the site and a sheaf of sets $F$ on $X$, subcanonicity [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-subcanonical], the adjunction defining $f^{-1}$, and the general Yoneda evaluation [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}h_V,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_V,f_*F)\cong(f_*F)(V)=F(X\times_YV)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_{X\times_YV},F).$$
The co-Yoneda assertion [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] therefore gives $f^{-1}h_V\cong h_{X\times_YV}$. Naturality in $V$ follows by evaluating both routes on the universal section: a map $V\to V'$ acts on the displayed chain by restriction along $X\times_YV\to X\times_YV'$. This calculation is for objects of the small site; it makes no assertion about representables whose structure morphisms are not weakly etale.

source.place: Tag 04D3, lemma-pullback-representable-sheaf; Tag 09A5 in proetale.tex, section-morphism; categories.tex Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda

proof.text: Roots of unity. Put $R=\mathbf Z[1/\ell]$, $N=\ell^n$ with $n\ge1$, $B_N=R[t]/(t^N-1)$, and $M_{N,Y}=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}B_N$, using [def-pc-fibre-product]. The map $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is obtained on affine opens by sending $1/\ell$ to the inverse of $\ell$; these maps glue. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a map from an affine test scheme to $\operatorname{Spec}B_N$ over $R$ is exactly an element $u$ with $u^N=1$; such an element is a unit with inverse $u^{N-1}$. For nonaffine test schemes these identifications glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Thus $h_{M_{N,Y}}$ is the underlying set sheaf of $\mu_{N,Y}$ of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Apply [lem-sbc-root-split-away-cover-etale] with $g=1$: its open $D(1)$ is the whole root scheme, so $R\to B_N$ is etale, hence ind-etale by the constant filtered diagram in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] and weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. Base change is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change], so $M_{N,Y}$ is a small-site object. Step 1 and the fibre-product universal property identify its inverse image with $h_{M_{N,X}}$, giving $c^f_N:f^{-1}\mu_{N,Y}\cong\mu_{N,X}$. The adjoint sends a root to its pullback, so this is precisely the map of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image]. Multiplication, the unit and power maps are maps between these representing objects and their finite products; inverse image preserves finite products by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. Consequently the comparison is a group isomorphism. More explicitly, for a local root $u$ and integer $a$, $c^f_N(u^a)=c^f_N(u)^a$, and for $N\mid N'$ the equality $(u|_{X\times_YV})^{N'/N}=(u^{N'/N})|_{X\times_YV}$ proves compatibility with all Kummer transitions and the constant-ring module actions. The case $n=0$ is the same construction with $t-1$: both sheaves are the zero abelian sheaf.

source.place: Tag 040M, example-roots-of-unity; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PK, section-kummer, root-algebra calculation; blueprint proof, Roots of unity

proof.text:
Finite coefficients. For the coefficient sheaves use $\alpha_f$ of [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. For finite constant rings its map agrees with the constant-section comparison: both adjoints send the constant element $a$ to the same constant element on a base-changed object, and sheafification makes that extension unique. This constant comparison is an isomorphism by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Interpret module pullback by [def-sfb-module-upper-star]; module objects can be read as sectionwise module sheaves by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Its sheafification hypothesis holds: [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor], with the constant integer presheaf as coefficient ring, identifies sheafification of a presheaf tensor with the tensor of its sheafifications; therefore tensoring carries a sheafification equivalence to a sheafification equivalence. The equivalence of module categories identifies the two tensor products, since both are sheafified sectionwise tensor products under this same comparison. Since $\alpha_f$ is invertible, extension of scalars along it merely identifies coefficients, so module pullback is the exact inverse image on underlying abelian sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. The relative tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] and Step 2 therefore give, if $\ell^rA=0$,
$$f^{-1}(\mu_{\ell^r,Y}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_Y}A_Y)\cong\mu_{\ell^r,X}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_X}A_X.$$
By [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] these are $f^{-1}A_Y(1)$ and $A_X(1)$. On local pure tensors the comparison sends $u\otimes a$ to $c^f_{\ell^r}(u)\otimes\alpha_f(a)$, so it is natural in homomorphisms of finite coefficient rings and compatible with reduction and Kummer maps. Independence of an annihilating exponent follows from [det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free] (2), and its compatibility follows from the same pure-tensor formula.

source.place: Finite A paragraph, with sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback

proof.text: Coefficient limits needed for the integral calculation. For a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, write $R_{E,S}=\mathcal O_{E,S}$ and $Q_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. The integral-limit assertion [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] identifies $R_{E,S}$ with $\varprojlim_m(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^m)_S$, and [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-pullback] (1) says that its canonical inverse-image comparison is $\alpha_f$. These assertions also hold for the $Q_n$ tower: [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] gives $\ell=u\pi_E^e$ for a unit $u$ and $e>0$ (positivity follows from $|\ell|_E<1$), hence $(\ell^n)=(\pi_E^{en})$. A compatible sequence at all $m$ restricts to the indices $en$; conversely, its $m$-th coordinate is the reduction of any coordinate at $en\ge m$, independent of that choice by compatibility. These mutually inverse formulas commute with every projection, so the same comparison $\alpha_f$ identifies $f^{-1}\varprojlim_n(Q_n)_Y$ with $\varprojlim_n(Q_n)_X$. Taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ includes $\mathbf Z_\ell$.

source.place: Integral twist paragraph: coefficient-limit identification; cofinal change from uniformizer powers to ell powers written out

proof.text:
Integral twist. Put $Q_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$, $M_n=(Q_n)_Y(1)$ and $L_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_n M_n$ [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. Apply [lem-pur-inverse-image-compatible-free-tower] to $u_f$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and $R_n=(Q_n)_Y$. Step 4 gives its coefficient comparison $\kappa$ and identifies it with $\alpha_f$. Clause (1) of [det-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free] supplies one cover $\widetilde Y\to Y$ and compatible $\zeta_n$. On its localized site, identified with $\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], the bases $b_n(a)=\zeta_n\otimes a$ identify $R_n$ with $M_n$ by the finite tensor construction of Step 3. Their transition identity is $t_n(\zeta_{n+1}\otimes a)=\zeta_n\otimes\bar a$. These are exactly the common-cover and compatible-basis hypotheses of the tower lemma. Its canonical comparison followed by the inverse limit of the compatible finite comparisons of Step 3 gives
$$c_E^f:f^{-1}L_{E,Y}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{E,X}.$$
It is semilinear over $\alpha_f$ and is characterized by all its projections, so it is independent of the generators and natural in coefficient homomorphisms. Each projection is the Step 3 map $u\otimes a\mapsto c^f_{\ell^n}(u)\otimes\alpha_f(a)$. Taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ includes $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)$.

source.place: Integral twist paragraph; apply the compatible-local-basis tower comparison after Steps 3 and 4.

proof.text: Rational and algebraically closed coefficients. By [sk-def-sp-tate-twist], $E_S(1)=L_{E,S}[1/\ell]$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,S}(1)=\varinjlim_E E_S(1)$, in the ambient sheaf categories. Write localization as the sequential colimit with transition multiplication by $\ell$. Inverse image preserves these colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], so applying it to the integral comparison in Step 5 gives $f^{-1}E_Y(1)\cong E_X(1)$. This includes $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. The maps for different $E$ commute with field inclusions: before localization and at every finite quotient the two maps send $\zeta_n\otimes a$ to $\zeta'_n\otimes a$, with $a$ taken through the specified coefficient homomorphism. Therefore these maps give an isomorphism on the filtered colimit defining the algebraic-closure twist. The indexing poset of finite subextensions is a set in the chosen coefficient universe, being a subset of the set of subfields of the fixed algebraic closure. The coefficient identifications on localization and on this filtered colimit are precisely those of [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-pullback] (2),(3), so all these twist comparisons are semilinear over $\alpha_f$. Here the algebraic-closure coefficient object is the finite-subextension condensed sheaf of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]; no assertion about all continuous functions with values in the topological algebraic closure or about a common-stage constructible category is used.

All signed powers. For $d=0$ the comparison is $\alpha_f$ [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. For $d>0$ the relative tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor], applied repeatedly to the comparison for $(1)$, gives the comparison for $d$ by [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. For $d<0$ put $L=\Lambda_Y(-d)$. The current ambient twist statement [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] explicitly states that $\Lambda_Y(1)$ is locally free of rank one on the compatible-generator cover for each admissible coefficient ring. On that cover a tensor power of its basis is a basis of $L$, so $L$ satisfies the finite locally free hypothesis of [lem-pur-ringed-site-finite-free-dual-pullback]. Apply that lemma to $R=\Lambda_Y$, $S=\Lambda_X$, $c=\alpha_f$ and this $L$. It identifies pullback of the negative twist $\mathcal Hom_R(L,R)$ with $\mathcal Hom_S(f^*L,S)$, which is $\Lambda_X(d)$ by the already proved positive comparison. As $\alpha_f$ is invertible, module pullback [def-sfb-module-upper-star] identifies with inverse image with transported coefficients. The dual comparison is defined by pullback of evaluation and sends the pulled-back dual basis to the dual of the pulled-back basis, as stated in the lemma. Thus the coefficient and Kummer compatibilities from the positive powers persist for the negative powers.

source.place: Powers and duals paragraph: finite locally free dual pullback, with ambient local freeness from the current twist definition.

proof.text:
Derived consequence on the entire ambient category. Let $R=\Lambda_Y$, $S=\Lambda_X$, and equip the geometric inverse image with the ring isomorphism $\alpha_f$. Its module pullback is the ringed-topos functor of [def-sfb-module-upper-star], identified with ordinary module-sheaf pullback by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. It is exact because the underlying inverse image is exact [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] and scalar extension along an isomorphism merely changes the name of the coefficient ring. It therefore induces $f^*$ on unbounded derived categories by termwise application, as in the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. In particular its value on $\Lambda_Y(d)[0]$ is $\Lambda_X(d)[0]$ by Step 7. Apply the unbounded ringed-topos derived tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] with $F=K$ and $G=\Lambda_Y(d)[0]$:
$$f^*(K(d))=Lf^*(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\Lambda_Y(d))\cong Lf^*K\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lf^*\Lambda_Y(d)\cong(f^*K)(d).$$
The twist notation is that of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. This requires no boundedness, constructibility, or finite-Tor hypothesis on $K$; the cited derived comparison already holds for all objects of $D(R)$.

split_report.blueprint: Steps 1-2: Roots of unity; Step 3: Finite A; Steps 4-5: Integral twist (compatible-basis tower lemma); Step 6: Rational and algebraic closure; Steps 7-8: Powers and duals (finite locally free dual pullback). Original unit route unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Step 3 uses its tensor/sheafification comparison to check that local equivalences are monoidal, the explicit hypothesis of the existing internal-module equivalence. This is a generic site tool, not a purity theorem; the unit has no tensor-sheafification interface.

Step 2 specializes the polynomial root-algebra theorem to g=1 and n=ell^r, showing that the explicit representing root scheme is an object of the small pro-etale site. It is a basic etaleness tool, not the smooth-base-change theorem of its unit.

Step 4 uses clause (5) and the absolute-value description of uniformizers to write ell=u*pi_E^e with e>0, then writes the cofinal coordinate formulas itself. The purity unit has no local-field valuation theorem.
Step 2 uses only the generic assertion that an ind-etale algebra is weakly etale, to put the etale root scheme on the small site. No proper-base-change conclusion is used.

Steps 2, 3, 6 and 8 use finite-limit preservation, exactness on abelian sheaves and colimit preservation of geometric inverse image. These are general site properties; no proper-base-change theorem replaces a step of the purity unit.

Step 8 applies the unbounded ringed-topos derived tensor comparison to K and the twist sheaf. This generic derived-category tool has the exact ambient scope needed here; the purity unit does not supply it.
Steps 3 and 7 need tensor pullback over the coefficient ring, rather than only tensor over the integers. This is a generic ringed-topos tool and does not introduce a proper-base-change argument.

Step 5 identifies the localized small pro-etale site at the compatible-generator cover with the small pro-etale site of that object, and identifies finite constant coefficient sheaves there. This generic site equivalence is not a geometric purity step.

Step 3 identifies the canonical finite constant-ring comparison and its action on constant sections. This supports the finite twist tensor calculation; the unit has no independent finite coefficient-sheaf comparison.
